newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit consolidation continues despite firm dlr.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit consolidation continues despite firm dlr.

text.p: The ringgit continued to consolidate after a partial recovery from recent declines, but it could fall again if the dollar/majors continue to remain firm, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the dollar's firmness after Bill Clinton's victory in the U.S. elections had little impact on the ringgit, which fell to 2.5275 before recovering to 2.5250/60 at 0800 GMT.
"There is some dollar/ringgit buying from Europe. Volumes are not large," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
He said any movement in the near-term is likely to be confined to the new range of 2.52-2.53.
The ringgit was trading in a 2.4950 to 2.5100 a dollar range until last week, when selling triggered by rumours and technical factors pulled it down to a seven-month low of 2.5330.
Dealers said the fall was mainly due to U.S. funds unwinding long ringgit/Singapore dollar positions, which had been completed.
However, many analysts and dealers have said that heavy dollar demand from Malaysian corporate sector would push the ringgit lower for the rest of the year.
"General sentiment is still biased towards a stronger dollar/ringgit," research firm I.D.E.A. said in a report.
